audit_note: The batch file stores correct_answer and explanation inline, so the key was visible on screen in the same read as the passage. Each item was worked from the passage first, but strictly speaking this was not a blind solve.

SEC10B-01.struck_how: No option is ill-formed on its own. 'which redistributes' and 'redistributing' are both legal fragments in isolation.
SEC10B-01.fix: Same option shape as 08 and 13 (sing finite / pl finite / -ing / which+V). Vary the nonfinite distractors, e.g. use 'having redistributed', or swap one for a tense distractor.

SEC10B-02.struck_how: All four are bare verb forms. None can be struck without the clause.
SEC10B-02.fix: This is a standard SAT shape. To reach hard, add a distractor such as 'and enabled' that is grammatical but makes a different construction, or one like 'which enabled' that tempts on meaning.

SEC10B-03.struck_how: None. Each option is a legal string on its own.
SEC10B-03.fix: 'to consult' and 'consulting' fall away at once once 'which a navigator' is read. Replace one with 'had consulted' versus 'consults' so that tense does some work. Minor: the explanation quotes 'its engraved scales', but the passage reads 'its finely engraved scales'.

SEC10B-04.struck_how: 'ornithologists logs' is a plural noun used attributively before a plural noun with no apostrophe. Edited text does not use that form.
SEC10B-04.fix: This is a 2x2 grid of possessive x number, and the key is the modal cell: 'ornithologists'' is in 2 options and 'log' is in 2, and they meet only at the key. Replace 'ornithologists logs' with 'ornithologist's logs' so that every value appears exactly twice and the modal heuristic finds no single cell.

SEC10B-05.struck_how: 'womens' is not a form edited text uses. In 'ledgers suggests' the subject-verb disagreement is visible inside the option itself. That leaves the key and 'woman's ledgers suggest'. The modal-token heuristic (women's in 2, suggest in 3) then picks the key.
SEC10B-05.fix: Drop it, or rebuild it so the verb is outside the option's internal subject. For example, make the blank only the possessive and noun ('women's ledgers' / 'womens' ledgers' / 'woman's ledgers' / 'womens ledgers'), and move agreement to a verb whose subject is set by the passage. As it stands, two distractors fail on their own text.

SEC10B-06.struck_how: All four are legal strings in isolation ('it's branching' = it is branching). But 'structure' immediately after the blank requires a possessive determiner and strikes both contractions, leaving 'its' or 'their'.
SEC10B-06.fix: The contraction distractors are dead once 'structure' is read, and its/it's is a well-drilled pair. For hard, make the antecedent truly ambiguous in number, e.g. a collective noun or 'the reef and its lagoon ... ' with 'its' versus 'their', so that the possessive form is not the whole item.

SEC10B-07.struck_how: None. All four are legal verb+object strings.
SEC10B-07.fix: This is a complete 2x2 (stores/store x them/it). The key is the cell that survives both axes, and the modal-token heuristic picks it with no passage. Collapse it to one axis: fix the pronoun outside the blank and test verb agreement, or vice versa. Then add a nonfinite or tense distractor. Note also that the nearest noun before the blank, 'week', is singular, so the 'agree with the nearest noun' error does not tempt here.

SEC10B-08.fix: A good item. It shares an option template with 01 and 13. Consider replacing 'which reshaped' with a tense distractor ('had reshaped') to break the shared shape.

SEC10B-09.struck_how: Both inverted verb+subject options carry their own agreement error inside the option: 'lie a sealed casket' and 'lies two sealed caskets'. That leaves the key and 'a sealed casket lying', and the 'finite verb wins' heuristic picks the key. 'whose lid', singular, also weighs against the plural casket.
SEC10B-09.fix: Drop it, or put the subject outside the blank. One way is a compound inverted subject: '... ______ a sealed casket and a bronze reliquary, whose lids bear ...' with lie/lies/lying/laying. The singular noun right after the verb then becomes the trap, and no option contains both verb and subject.

SEC10B-10.fix: The true subject 'panels' sits right next to the blank and the attractor is far away. That reverses the usual trap and makes the item easy. To reach hard, place a singular noun between 'panels' and the blank, e.g. 'the smaller altar panels beside the apse ______'. The option set {has X, have X, X-ing, to X} is identical to 12's.

SEC10B-11.struck_how: None. All four are legal forms.
SEC10B-11.fix: Simple past inside a clearly past narrative is easy. For hard, test past perfect against simple past, e.g. a later frame such as 'By the time his superiors dismissed him, he ______ students to wash...' with 'had required' as the key and 'required' as the strong distractor.

SEC10B-12.fix: 'The number of' (singular) versus 'a number of' (plural) is a well-known rule, so many prepared students spot it. Its option shape is identical to 10's. Vary the distractors, e.g. replace 'to decline' with 'had declined' so the 'since' clause has to be read for tense.

SEC10B-13.fix: This is the strongest item in the half. It shares an option template with 01 and 08.

cross_item_tells: Finite-verb template: 01, 08, 10, 12 and 13 all take the form 'long subject + attractor, blank = main verb' with options {singular finite, plural finite, -ing participle, which-clause or to-infinitive}. Striking the two nonfinite options leaves a coin flip on number on all 5, so the heuristic narrows rather than decides. The options of 10 and 12 match in shape ({has X, have X, X-ing, to X}), as do those of 01, 08 and 13. 02 is the only item whose key is nonfinite, which partly offsets this.
'The key agrees with a noun far from the blank, never the nearest noun' picks the key on 01, 08, 12 and 13 (4 items). 10 breaks it: the true subject is adjacent. 09 and 07 are neutral.

Modal-token heuristic (pick the option whose components appear most often across the set) decides 04, 05, 07 and 09 and is right on all 4. 07 is a complete 2x2 grid, and 04 is a 2x2 with one cell replaced by a no-apostrophe form.

Options carrying their own agreement error: 05 ('ledgers suggests') and 09 ('lie a sealed casket', 'lies two sealed caskets') can be cut to two options without the passage. With modal or finite tie-breaks, all of 05 and 09 is decided.
drop: SEC10B-05: 2 of 3 distractors can be struck from the option text alone ('womens'; 'ledgers suggests'), and the modal-token heuristic picks the key from the remaining two.
SEC10B-09: 2 of 3 distractors carry their own inverted agreement error, and the 'finite verb wins' heuristic picks the key from the remaining two.
summary: All 13 keys match, and all are exclusive with no second defensible option. All items are on the blueprint (06 and 07 use pronoun-antecedent agreement, which is on the SEC list). Explanations are student-facing, quote options and address every distractor. The only blemish is a small misquote in 03. Two drops (05, 09) for options-only leaks. Main cross-item tells: the modal-token/2x2 heuristic decides 04, 05, 07 and 09, and the shared finite-verb option template reduces 5 items to a number-agreement coin flip. Difficulty does not match the 'hard' label: hard 2 (08, 13), medium 6 (01, 02, 03, 04, 07, 12), easy 5 (05, 06, 09, 10, 11).
